title: Gehl Place and Windom Road development approvals
subtitle: Official Plan update launched; Lower Doon appeal settlement and City land environmental agreement authorized after closed session.
overview: At a special meeting chaired by Acting Mayor Singh, with the Mayor absent, Council approved two development applications and started a full rewrite of the city's Official Plan. The Gehl Place zoning change was approved as amended at the Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee earlier that day {{vote:m2}}. For 32-42 Windom Road, Council adopted an Official Plan amendment allowing a multiple residential development with a floor space ratio of 1.4 and a height of 15.1 metres, and approved the matching zoning change {{vote:m3}}. The Official Plan amendment goes to the Region of Waterloo for approval.
Council also directed staff to begin work on a new Official Plan for Kitchener {{vote:m4}}. That plan will guide where and how the city grows.

After a closed session, Council authorized the CAO to sign documents accepting terms on the environmental condition of City-owned land {{vote:m5}}. It also authorized the City Solicitor to settle an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal about the Lower Doon zoning by-law {{vote:m6}}. Two councillors declared conflicts on the appeal because of Conestoga College's proximity to the site, and did not take part. Council then passed the related by-laws.

decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning by-law amendment for Kitchener Green Developments Inc., as amended at committee, with no further public notice required.

Council adopted an Official Plan amendment for a site-specific policy area allowing a floor space ratio of 1.4 and a height of 15.1 metres, sent it to the Region for approval, and approved the related zoning change.
Council directed staff to start work on a comprehensive new Official Plan for Kitchener.

decisions.item: Environmental site condition on City land
decisions.detail: Council authorized the CAO to sign correspondence or an agreement accepting the terms on the environmental condition of City land, as directed in closed session.
Council authorized the City Solicitor to settle Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal 23-001308 on Zoning By-law 2023-156 for Lower Doon, as directed in closed session.

debate: The transcript records little discussion of the planning items. The committee chair brought forward the three planning recommendations together, and they were moved and voted on without recorded debate.
No delegates or public speakers appear in the transcript, so it contains no resident concerns about the Gehl Place or Windom Road proposals.
On the Lower Doon appeal, two councillors stated conflicts of interest tied to Conestoga College's closeness to the site. Council confirmed the conflict was noted before the vote.
The clerk advised that the by-laws for the planning approvals, including the Gehl Place amendment, were formally added to the agenda late.
